gap: No result ChatGPT got states the price per Wh of any ALLPOWERS 1.5 kWh kit. At our link price the S2000 Pro + 200 W kit works out to $0.42–0.52 per rated Wh, against $0.91 for Jackery's 1500 Ultra + 200 W kit. No result mentions that StorageReview drew only 920 Wh from an S2000 Pro. Even after that cut, the kit that ships now costs $0.83 per measured Wh.
standout_why: PowerSized (solar-generator-kits, cited in chat 1) lists only three kits between 1.2 and 1.8 kWh, all Jackery 1,536 Wh. It gives refill hours and station-only weight but no price per Wh for kits and no measured usable capacity. StormWatts (cited in chat 2) has kit $/kWh, panel $/W (kit minus station) and refill on a 4.5-sun-hour day, but no kit between 1,264 and 2,042 Wh, so nothing near 1,500 Wh. Neither rival lists an ALLPOWERS S2000 or S2000 Pro kit, and neither compares measured with rated capacity. Our own panels-included page could not be read: the TLS certificate check failed when fetching it.
decides: This confirms an ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro kit as the value pick at 1,500 Wh. The S2000 Pro + SE200, which ships now, is $759.24 at our link: $0.52 per rated Wh. Even at StorageReview's 920 Wh measurement it is $0.83 per Wh, below the Jackery 1500 Ultra kit's $0.91 per rated Wh. At the rated capacity both 200 W kits need the same ~7.5 h of full sun to refill. Jackery keeps the case for a shopper who weighs a measured 1.3–1.5 kWh delivered, IP65 build (Ultra) and maker support above price. The S2000 Pro + SF200 ($612.90, pre-order Nov 19) and S2000 + SF200 ($612.90, pre-order Nov 20) are the cheapest per Wh for a shopper who can wait a few days.
